text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Rabobank and unions agree that 4,000 of the bank's 29,000 employees will be offered a chance to re-train or leave. (p1)
- Dutch central bank DNB is expected to raise money market rates this week. (p1)
- Property fund Rodamco forecasts a 20 percent increase in net profit this year. (p1)
- Flour, mixed feed and bakeries group Meneba expects to be relaunched on the Amsterdan bourse after buying out its Australian owner. (p1)
- Central planning bureau CPB sees exports grow to almost double that in 1996 over the next two years. (p1)
- Textile maker Textielgroep Twenthe manages to cut losses from 10 million guilders in 1995 to 546,000 in 1996. (p3)
- Ten Cate (plastics, rubber and textiles) posts 30.2 million guilders 1996 net from 20.5 million in 1995. (p4)
- Green funds attract one billion guilders from investors in the past two years. (p15)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Dutch ice-skating team wins 13 medals (four golds) at world championship in Warsaw. (p1)
- Postal arm of Dutch PTT KPN buys 60 pct stake in Belgium's loyalty programmes maker Countdown Benelux. (p2)
- Storage firm Pakhoed takes 50 pct interest in Britain's agency firm Genchem. (p2)
- South Limburg's city of Geleen demands clarification from chemicals concern DSM about benzene spillage last year. (p3)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Surinam calls back its ambassador from the Netherlands because of tightenend drugs control at Schiphol airport of Paramaribo flights. (p1)
- Central planning bureau CPB forecasts stronger job growth than expected. (p13)
- Unions divided over large bonus for Philips Electronics' chiefs. (p15)
- "Mister" project that uses IT technology for Rotterdam Port allied small and medium-sized businesses is successful. TROUW
- Environmental minister Margaretha de Boer only opts for another term, if environmental pact is included in coalition agreement. (p1)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Polluted soil at some 400 train stations will cost Dutch Rail NS three to four billion guilders. (p3)
- Food concern CSM takes over the Scandinavian Malaco group. (p11)
